newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 33,600 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 42.295 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 22,000 tonnes, in the U.K. 9,000 and in Belgium 2,600 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 2.219 million tonnes. This compares with the 58,500 tonnes awarded on June 12, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 2.321 million tonnes.

Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-September to be 42.295 Ecus per 100 kilos of sugar -- the exact amount awarded.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 30,000 and 60,000 tonnes versus 87,750 last week when the restitution was 41.653 Ecus.
